summary: Credential-claim translation failure prevents Dedicated deployer from assuming prod deployer role
description:
Issue summary: After an org-policy rollforward, the Dedicated provisioning pipeline fails to assume the per-tenant deployer role in prod accounts. The STS assume-role call returns AccessDenied due to missing session tags/claims that our role condition requires.

Impact: Dedicated customer onboards and CI-driven deploys to prod are blocked for a subset of tenants (approx. 6 customers). Automatic provisioning and emergency rollouts fail; engineers must perform manual escalation to use a fallback path.

Environment: prod (multi-account), dedicated provisioner service running in us-east and eu-west clusters. Affected tenants appear across us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

Observed behavior: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity and AssumeRole calls from the dedicated-provisioner are rejected with IAM condition mismatch referencing tag:user_env and tag:team. The auth logs show that incoming session tags were present at the WIF entrypoint but were stripped before the STS call.

Expected behavior: Session tags propagated by the federated identity exchange should be preserved so that role condition policies in the customer account match and the assume-role succeeds.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger dedicated onboarding pipeline for a new tenant with default deployer role mapping
Pipeline calls the org federated-identity service to exchange GCP WIF token for AWS temporary credentials
Federation service issues STS:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity with session tags, then calls AssumeRole into tenant account
Observe AccessDenied from tenant account with IAM condition mismatch referencing tags
logs: 2026-03-10T02:14:23Z dedicated-provisioner: sts:AssumeRole target=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/tenant-deployer AccessDenied: Failed IAM condition: Missing required tag user_env
comments: 2026-03-10 08:47 - Connor Hayes: I started a capture of federation exchange headers and confirmed session tag present at federation gateway but absent on outbound AWS AssumeRole call. Suspect token translation layer is normalizing/stripping attributes.
2026-03-10 11:22 - Maya Chen: Noted that org-policy tag-enforcement rollout happened 2026-03-09; could be coincidental but matches timeframe. Adding iam and federation teams.

2026-03-11 09:04 - SRE Oncall: Temporarily added an allowlist exception to tenant account role condition for affected tenants to unblock emergency deploys; this is a temporary mitigation and must be reverted once root cause is fixed.

2026-03-12 15:30 - Connor Hayes: Reproduced in staging with debug flags; narrowing to the token-translator microservice which dropped custom claim namespaces when strict claim-sanitizer enabled. Creating PR to preserve namespaced claims for 'redwood:*' keys. See PR link below.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: org-policy rollforward tightened allowed session tags and our federated identity broker started stripping tags that don't match a new whitelist.

Confirmed: GCP WIF token contains attributes under 'redwood:env' and 'redwood:team'. Federation gateway maps these to session tags 'user_env' and 'team' correctly. The token-translator microservice applies a sanitizer which removes nonstandard claim namespaces when 'strict_claims' toggle is true.
Reproduction: Toggle strict_claims=false in staging translator service; assume-role flow preserves tags and tenant role assumption succeeds.

Root cause: release 2026-03-08 to token-translator enabled strict claim sanitization to harden against malicious upstream claims. The sanitizer incorrectly treated 'redwood:' namespace as nonstandard and removed it, which removed tags used by customer account IAM conditions.
Related signals: Increase in onboarding failures correlated with deploy of translator v1.7.3; CloudTrail shows MissingTag condition failures starting at 2026-03-09T21:00Z.
resolution:
Hotfix: rolled back token-translator v1.7.3 to v1.7.2 for prod federation gateways at 2026-03-12T04:20Z which restored session tag propagation. Deployed PR preserving 'redwood:' namespace and added an allowlist entry to sanitizer. Tenant onboarding flows returned to green.

Root cause: claim sanitizer in token-translator mistakenly removed namespaced claims used to populate AWS session tags.

Permanent fix: PR merged to token-translator adds explicit preservation of 'redwood:' and 'org:' namespaces and a unit test asserting tag propagation; will release v1.7.4 after QA.
follow_up_actions: Ship token-translator v1.7.4 with tests and staged rollout (Connor H, release manager)
Audit other microservices for strict_claims toggle impact and add integration test covering end-to-end federation->tenant assume-role flow (SRE + Auth team)
Revoke temporary allowlist exceptions in tenant accounts and verify IAM logs for normal assume-role success (Security Ops)
Add dashboard alert for sudden rise in IAM MissingTag errors correlated to federation releases
